newsitem.title: USA: Harvard says pursuing sale of units.
newsitem.headline: Harvard says pursuing sale of units.

text.p: Harvard Industries Inc, which filed for bankruptcy protection in May, said Thursday it is continuing to pursue the sale of its Doehler-Jarvis, Harman Automotive and Harvard Interiors subsidiaries.

The company said it has hired investment advisors Stump and Co to sell Harvard Interiors and has received an unsolicited proposal regarding the materials handling division of its Kingston-Warren unit. It said it is evaluating and negotiating the proposal.
It said that if no deal for the sale of Harman Automotive is consummated, it would look into the feasibility of liquidating the subsidiary.

The company disclosed its plans as it reported a consolidated net loss for its third fiscal quarter of 1997 ended June 30 of $29.99 million or $4.27 per common share, compared with a loss of $14.8 million or $2.12 per common shares a year ago.
Consolidated net sales for the latest quarter were $217.9 million compared with $222.3 million for the 1996 quarter.
The company said that as has been the case historically, its fourth quarter will be adversely affected by customer plant shutdowns for vacations and changeover to new models.

It said it is in talks with the agent for its debtor-in-possession (DIP) lending syndicate to obtain consent to exceed the $10 million limitation on capital expenditures for the period May 8 to September 30.

It said it expects to be in compliance with the required $11 million cumulative consolidated earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA) under its DIP financing agreement for the five months ending September 30, 1997.
It said that as of June 30, it had borrowed $3.9 million under its DIP revolving credit line, its letters of credit outstanding were $12.2 million and the DIP term loan was $65.0 million.
The DIP financing will enable it to continue normal opertions during the chapter 11 bankruptcy proceedings, it said.
